info.title: Judgment Pack Runner local pilot
info.description: Single local installation owner, one fixed pack release per job. Durable local schedules, file changes and authenticated event admission. Experimental evaluator; no external actions. Direct runner prefix /v1; owner-authenticated Desk proxy /api/operations.

get.description: Trusted installation profiles and canonical digests. Read-only; profile installation is host configuration.

Offline input lineage bundle. Trust the profiles and release digest independently. Does not establish sealed-session completeness or policy truth. Version 2, 3, 4 or 5 may be asked for, at most once (none asked is 2), and the run is served at the highest version up to the one asked whose material it holds, answered 200 either way, so read version from the body: version 3 adds the audit record's original bytes, version 4 also the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, and version 5 also the record's signature sidecar. A run the store no longer holds, whose entry the chain still names, is answered with 410 run_not_held, naming the entry's sequence. A run of a job with no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping, has no lineage: it is served from version 3 on, by the same steps, with inputs: not-mapped and no preparation, and is refused with 422 not_verified_mapping when it holds no audit record's bytes or version 2 (or none) is asked.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The export version asked for, at most once, in a well-formed query. Without it, or with 2: version 2, unchanged. With 3: version 3 when the run holds its audit record's bytes, and version 2 for a run that holds none (recorded before Runner kept them, or without an audit record). With 4: version 4 when the run also has an entry in the installation's chain of runs, and otherwise what 3 serves: a run recorded before Runner chained its runs has no entry and is unchained. With 5: version 5 when the run also keeps the signature sidecar of its audit record, and otherwise what 4 serves: a run recorded without a signing key, by a Runtime that cannot sign, or before Runner kept the sidecar, is unsigned. Anything else, or a malformed query, is refused with invalid_version. A run without lineage (no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping) has no version-2 export: with none or 2 it is refused with 422 not_verified_mapping, and with 3, 4 or 5 it is served as above, from version 3.

422.description: not_verified_mapping: the run's job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping, so its export has no lineage, and the run holds no audit record's bytes (it failed, was interrupted, expired or has not finished, or was recorded before Runner kept them) or version 2, or none, was asked. Message: "This run does not use mapping v2, and an export without lineage carries the audit record's bytes: ask for version 3, 4 or 5 of a completed run that holds them."

parameters.name: stream
parameters.description: The stream the Runtime wrote when it evaluated the run, at most once in a well-formed query. Anything else is refused with 400 invalid_stream.

get.description: A finished run's attempt diagnostics: what its Runtime wrote to standard error, or standard output, when it evaluated the run, as written, up to the first 65,536 bytes (cut before a character the bound would split). A run still queued or running is refused with 409 run_not_finished. A run whose stream is not retained answers 404 no_diagnostics, with its state and what the store records of it (it expired in the queue, or never started); a missing file is never taken to say the Runtime did not run. The stream is read through the attempts directory Runner holds, and Runner serves only the file it looked at and then opened: the run's directory and the stream are each looked at without following a link, and checked on the opened descriptor to be that same object, a directory or a regular file private to the operator. A link when Runner looks, a file or directory others may read, or a name that resolves to any other object when opened is refused with 500 diagnostics_refused, and nothing of it is served; a name that vanishes in between answers 404. The Runtime's own words, kept in the operator's store: they explain a run and establish nothing about it. A read writes no entry in the journal of job activity.

X-Diagnostics-Bytes.description: The whole stream's size in bytes.

X-Diagnostics-Truncated.description: Whether the answer is shorter than the stream.

get.description: The installation's chain of runs: every entry's line, exactly as stored, each ended by a newline, in sequence order. An entry binds one completed run's id to the SHA-256 of its audit record's exact bytes, chained by the Runtime's rules (trail, sequence, previous over the exact bytes of the line before). It is a trail file as the Runtime's audit verify reads one, and verify-run --chain reads it. Read in pages, as it stood at some moment during the reading; a failure after the answer began aborts the transfer. The operator keeps the chain: against the operator it establishes nothing without a checkpoint held independently.

200.description: The chain, one entry per line

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Later than: the sequence of the last entry read, or 0, the default, from the start. Unlike run and occurrence lists, which page newest first, the journal pages oldest first, as the chain of runs is read.

get.description: A job's entries in the journal of job activity: those naming the job, and those naming its release alone (its preview, a refused creation). Entries are oldest first, at most 50 after the cursor, in the order their changes committed. A reader that has caught up asks again with next. The operator's own log: not chained, not signed, and binding nothing against the operator. A job the store does not hold is answered 404 not_found.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Later than: the sequence of the last entry read, or 0, the default, from the start. Unlike run and occurrence lists, which page newest first, the journal pages oldest first, as the chain of runs is read.

parameters.name: job
parameters.description: Only the entries the job's route serves, those naming the job and those naming its release alone, and Runner's own (journal.began, runner.started, runner.stopped), which concern no job but explain a gap in every job's. A job the store does not hold is answered 404 not_found.

get.description: Every entry of the journal of job activity, including those that concern no job: Runner's own, a release never made into a job, a refusal that names nothing else. Entries are oldest first, at most 50 after the cursor, in the order their changes committed. A reader that has caught up asks again with next. The operator's own log: not chained, not signed, and binding nothing against the operator.

post.description: Verify and derive a mapping v2 prefix. Returns the next instantiated acquisition request, or complete prepared input. Accepts source-only partial input; checks every trusted profile and class admission before returning any request. Performs no network calls, evaluation or persistence.

post.description: Direct Runner requires owner bearer plus X-Trigger-Token. Desk exposes POST /api/job-events/{trigger} using only Authorization: Bearer <trigger-token>; browser Origin is refused. New deliveries must be no older than 5 minutes, at most 30 seconds in the future. Exact retries return the original occurrence; changed payloads with the same ID conflict. Accepted work may be skipped by overlap/queue policy: inspect occurrence.state. The token that created an occurrence can read its result with readEventResult.

get.description: The one read a trigger token has: an occurrence that this token itself created, its state and, once its run completed, the disposition and handoff target. No inputs, identifiers of other records, problem text or listing. Direct Runner requires owner bearer plus X-Trigger-Token; Desk does not expose this route yet. A token that is not the trigger's current credential (wrong, rotated or absent) returns 401 invalid_trigger_token. A current token asking for an occurrence it did not create (another trigger's, one created by an earlier token of this trigger, or one accepted before this read existed) returns 404 occurrence_not_found, the same answer as for an occurrence that does not exist.

post.summary: Stop waiting and fence late results; provider cancellation is best effort.
Check the original source operation IDs again, without extending deadlines or replaying uncertain provider calls.

preparation.description: Server-computed for v2; never trusted from a caller.

Input.description: Manual facts/evidence, v1 selected file, or ordered v2 case/file/MCP mapping. Omit facts/evidence to use projection; supplied values must match. V2 verification requires installation profiles.

matrix.description: Optional serialized Runtime matrix with saved expectations. Omit only when no saved tests exist. It is evaluated afresh against the frozen pack and Runtime.

CreateJob.description: Requires explicit review. Only passed checks and explicitly reviewed not-run releases are admitted. Failed, incomplete or mismatched test evidence returns 409 release_not_ready. An installation booted with requireTestedReleases refuses a new job from a not-run release with 409 release_untested; repeating the creation of an existing job still returns it. Coverage never gates. Reusing an immutable release and name is idempotent.

auditBytes.description: The audit record exactly as the Runtime wrote it, without the newline that ends its line, in standard base64: the bytes a digest of the record, such as a gateway receipt's decision.recordDigest, is taken over. audit is the same record parsed, which Runner encodes again with other bytes. Every run Runner now records completed has them: an evaluation whose trail is not that one line, ended by a newline, is refused and its run fails. Absent for a run recorded before Runner kept them, for one Runner 0.4.0 completed without them, and for a run that did not complete. Not in run lists or briefs.

auditSignatures.description: The signature sidecar of the attempt's audit trail, signatures.jsonl, exactly as the Runtime wrote it, newlines included, in standard base64: the line signing the audit record, when the installation gave the Runtime a signing key (signingKey on the boot line) and it could sign. At most 16 KiB. Absent for a run recorded without a key, by a Runtime that cannot sign, or before Runner kept the sidecar; such a run is unsigned. What it holds is checked only by verify-run --public-key. Not in run lists or briefs.

interruptedAt.description: When Runner saw this run stop, at an orderly stop: the moment the evaluation it was in was cancelled. finishedAt keeps its meaning, the time Runner recorded the run's end. A run found running at a restart has none, since Runner did not see it stop: its run.interrupted journal entry gives the window the stop lies in. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports, whose version-2 readers decode strictly.

reason.description: Why a run ended without an evaluation, as a code: queue-expired, for an automatic run whose queue time ran out before the dispatcher reached it. Its state stays failed, and its problem the sentence it was. Absent for every other run, and for a run that expired before Runner kept the code. Served with the run and in run lists; not in verification exports.

report.description: Retained Runtime packs test outputVersion 2, including rows and advisory coverage. Incomplete invocations may retain a diagnostic report.

mappingDigest.description: Runner-computed mapping digest; if supplied it must match.

SourceSnapshot.description: Retained JSON file (200,000 decoded bytes maximum). local-file requires selectedAt and forbids proof. google-drive requires the existing Desk DocumentObject proof with Drive selection, receipt response and sealed registry. Runner checks structural/byte binding, not cryptographic authenticity; consumers verify with their configured pin. No provider credentials. Snapshot max 1 MiB.

proof.description: Existing signed document acquisition and sealed registry contract; required for Google Drive.

factsText.description: Exact mapped facts JSON for consumers that cannot represent all JSON numbers losslessly.

evidenceText.description: Exact availability JSON; empty if omitted.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

source.description: JSON Pointer in the input object, or empty for the root.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

target.description: Non-root JSON Pointer destination. Targets must not overlap.

source.description: JSON Pointer in the input object, or empty for the root.

arguments.description: Frozen template; whole-value $param and integer-only $text. runAt is derivation-only.

receipt.description: Complete signed Gateway v3 acquisition receipt; Runner verifies the signed fields, profile and canonical result.

VerificationBundle.description: Version 2, the export Runner has always made. It carries no original bytes of the audit record.

VerificationBundleV3.description: Version 3: version 2 with the audit record's bytes, as run.auditBytes, beside the parsed run.audit. Only a completed run that holds them is exported as version 3. verify-run checks that the bytes parse to run.audit and reports their SHA-256, the digest a gateway receipt would name for those bytes; that they are the bytes the Runtime wrote for this run is shown only by comparison with a digest held independently, such as a receipt's. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes member, whose bytes are held to 8 MiB.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

VerificationBundleV4.description: Version 4: version 3 with the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, as chain. Only a completed run that holds its audit record's bytes and has an entry is exported as version 4. verify-run checks that the entry names this run and the SHA-256 of run.auditBytes, and that the checkpoint is the entry's; along a supplied chain and against checkpoints held independently of the operator, it checks the entry's place in the chain. Without a held checkpoint it establishes nothing against the operator, who keeps the chain. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes and chain members; the entry is held to 1024 bytes. It carries no run.auditSignatures, which only version 5 does.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

VerificationBundleV5.description: Version 5: version 4 with the signature sidecar of the run's audit record, as run.auditSignatures. Only a completed run that has an entry in the installation's chain of runs and keeps a sidecar is exported as version 5. verify-run --public-key checks the record's signature under the key it is given, held first to the key check (no key of small order, no non-canonical encoding), by the Runtime guide's rule with the attempt's one-record trail known; --require-signed refuses a run that no valid signature covers. A valid signature shows only that whoever held the key signed these exact bytes: nothing against the operator, who holds the key, and nothing once the key is copied. Held to 8 MiB beside the run.auditBytes, chain and run.auditSignatures members; the sidecar is held to 16 KiB.

inputs.description: Present only in the export of a run whose job has no input mapping, or a v1 file mapping: the run has no lineage, and its run.input has no preparation. Absent from a mapping-v2 run's export. verify-run checks such an export's bytes, chain entry and signature as any export's, and in place of lineage that the release froze no mapping v2, the run names the release and its mapping, and the audit record evaluated the run's facts and evidence with no citation; it reports inputs: not-mapped and no targetsByClass.

RunChainExport.description: A run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, and that entry's checkpoint, which a holder keeps. The checkpoint is a function of the entry's bytes.

entry.description: The entry's line exactly as stored, in standard base64: one JSON object of entryVersion "1", trail (32 lowercase hex characters), sequence (from 1), previous (the SHA-256 of the line before it, or of nothing for the first), kind "run", run (the run's id) and auditDigest (the SHA-256 of the run's audit record's exact bytes), in that order as Runner writes it. Read by its members, as JSON reads them.

Checkpoint.description: The Runtime's checkpoint (ADR-0047): a chain's identity, an entry's sequence, and the SHA-256 of that entry's exact line bytes. Its compact encoding, members in this order, is its RFC 8785 canonical form.

Schedule.description: Intervals use elapsed time. Calendar schedules skip nonexistent local times and choose the first repeated time. End is exclusive. Kind-specific fields are mutually exclusive.

value.description: Exact JSON Input envelope; constants only. Source responses and computed preparation are forbidden.

path.description: Project-relative JSON input envelope or v2 case file.

AutomaticInput.description: mapped-sources supports v2 local files and installed Gateway operations. Retained source responses and interactive file grants are never reused.

preparationSeconds.description: Omit or use 0 for one hour on durable connections. Explicit waits require mapped-sources and all operation profiles installed as durable.

TriggerConfig.description: Event triggers take inputs from each delivery and forbid schedule/input/watch fields. Schedules require schedule and input. File triggers require a watched path used by their file inputs and a stability delay. Cloud triggers require cloud and input and forbid schedule/watch fields. For cloud, missed=latest delivers every signal before expiry; expiry starts at scheduledAt.

token.description: Plaintext only when first enabling an event or rotating its credential; otherwise empty. Never retrievable later.

SourcePreparation.description: Public progress only. Checkpoint bytes, frozen operation requests and installed Gateway URLs remain private.

run.description: Present once the occurrence has a run.

CalculatorPin.description: The installation's statement that each allowed tool computes a deterministic function of the inputs it echoes and the tables it reports, calling no model. Only on a record MCP profile.

CalculationBinding.description: Required exactly when the operation's profile names a calculator. Binds each echoed input to a parameter of the source (never runAt) and each reported table to its maximum age in seconds.

CalculationInput.description: An input the calculator echoed, the parameter it is bound to, and where that parameter's value came from: the case or an earlier source, and the pointer.

JournalActor.description: Who Runner can say initiated a change. Never a person: Runner cannot know one. installation is whoever holds the owner bearer, named by the boot line's owner; a trigger acts at a revision; a trigger-credential is an event delivery whose X-Trigger-Token was the trigger's current key, named by the revision the key was issued at (null for a key issued before the journal began), never by the token or its digest; a delivery refused after its credential was authenticated is that credential's, as it was then, even if the key is rotated before the refusal is recorded; a cloud-connection is a cloud signal Runner discarded; runner is Runner itself.

JournalConcerns.description: The ids a change is about, each present only where it applies. An entry that names a job also names its release.

JournalInterruption.description: An interruption's own time. seen true: Runner saw the stop, at at. seen false: Runner found the work at a restart and cannot know when it stopped; it was running at lastKnownRunning, the last time Runner recorded it alive (absent when the journal holds no such time), and had stopped by the restart, the runner.started entry at sequence restart.

JournalEntry.description: One entry of the journal of job activity (docs/design/activity-journal.md): one change of state Runner made, written in the transaction that made it, or a refused request to start work. The operator's own log: not chained, not signed, and binding nothing against the operator. It holds no inputs, secrets, tokens or digests of either. The members after reason are particular to kinds, as their descriptions say; a member added later raises entryVersion.

sequence.description: The entry's place in the journal, from 1, in the order changes committed: the cursor.

at.description: When Runner wrote the entry, by its own clock. Order is sequence, never at.

revision.description: The trigger revision: after the change, for a change of a trigger; the one an occurrence was admitted under, for the occurrence and its run.

from.description: The record's state before the change, for triggers (paused or enabled), occurrences and runs; null when the change created the record. Absent for a kind that concerns no record with a state.

to.description: The record's state after the change. Absent for a kind that concerns no record with a state.

reason.description: The reason or problem text Runner recorded with the change, where the record serves one, cut at 1,024 bytes; for a discarded cloud signal, the reason Runner gives.

previousRevision.description: trigger.*: the trigger's revision before the change; null for a new trigger. The values of both are the trigger's snapshots, never copied here.

keyIssued.description: trigger.resumed: the event trigger's first key was issued at this revision. The key is in the answer to the request, never here.

nextAt.description: trigger.resumed, for a schedule: its next time.

occurrenceKind.description: An occurrence's admission (from null): the kind of trigger it came from.

scheduledAt.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

missedFrom.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

missedThrough.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

expiresAt.description: An occurrence's admission: as the occurrence holds it.

deadline.description: occurrence.preparing, for a durable preparation: its deadline.

readyUntil.description: occurrence.ready, for a durable preparation: until when its run may be admitted.

chainSequence.description: run.completed: the sequence of the run's entry in the installation's chain of runs, appended in the same transaction.

runtimeDigest.description: release.previewed: the release's Runtime; runner.started: the Runtime this process pinned.

tests.description: release.previewed: the state of the release's saved tests.

request.description: admission.refused: the request refused. A refusal's entry is best effort: if the store cannot write it, the refusal is answered as it was and has no entry.

status.description: admission.refused: the HTTP status the request was answered with. Absent for a cloud signal.

code.description: admission.refused: the error code the request was answered with. Absent for a cloud signal.

coalescedSeconds.description: admission.refused: identical refusals in this many seconds after the entry are not entries.

held.description: journal.began: what the store held when its journal began, none of which has an entry.

journalBegan.description: When the store's journal began. Nothing before it has an entry, and nothing is back-filled.

next.description: The sequence of the page's last entry, or the cursor given when the page is empty: the after of the next request. It never resets to 0.
